\[
J(x) = \frac{\sum_{d \ne 0} I(x + d) \, e^{-\frac{\lvert d \rvert^2}{2\sigma^2} - \frac{(I(x + d) - I(x))^2}{t^2}}}{\sum_{d \ne 0} e^{-\frac{\lvert d \rvert^2}{2\sigma^2} - \frac{(I(x + d) - I(x))^2}{t^2}}}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(J(x)\): The result at pixel x
- \(I\): The image channel
- \(d\): The offset of a neighbor
- \(\sigma\): The spatial sigma
- \(t\): The brightness threshold

Each neighbor x + d gets a weight that falls with its distance, by a Gaussian of sigma. It also falls with the brightness difference from the center, by a Gaussian of the threshold t. So the neighbors that count are those on the same side of an edge, the univalue segment of Smith and Brady. The sums leave out d = 0, the center itself. So a single noisy pixel is replaced by its similar neighbors, or, when none is similar enough that a weight remains, by the median of its 8 neighbors.
